content.user_title: Review Django Code Like a Strict Backend Engineer
content.value_statement: Backend reviews often miss tenant scoping, migration safety, and contract risks. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a strict Django review checklist.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Django backend changes using a correctness-first priority order.
Checks multi-tenant scoping, permissions, exports, and auditability concerns.
Flags unsafe Django migrations and recommends safer rollout patterns.
Evaluates tests for edge cases, regressions, and realistic fixtures.
Applies SOLID principles through focused review checklists and examples.
Produces structured Markdown reviews with strengths, issues, tests, and verdicts.
limitations: It is tuned for Django and Python backend repositories.
It does not replace running the project test suite.
It may be too strict for quick exploratory reviews.
It needs repository context to cite exact files and lines.

use_cases.title: Review a Django pull request
use_cases.description: Use it before merge to find tenant scoping, data integrity, migration, and test coverage issues.

use_cases.title: Audit a backend refactor
use_cases.description: Use it to check that refactors preserve contracts, reduce complexity, and keep behavior easy to test.

use_cases.title: Improve review consistency
use_cases.description: Use it to standardize review language, severity tags, and quality expectations across backend changes.

prompt_templates.title: Basic PR Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the monty-code-review skill to review this Django pull request. Focus on correctness, security, tests, and migration safety.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Risk Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the monty-code-review skill for a quick pass. Only flag blocking and should-fix issues, and suppress minor nits.

prompt_templates.title: Migration Safety Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the monty-code-review skill to review these Django model and migration changes. Focus on rollout safety and production data risk.

prompt_templates.title: SOLID Refactor Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the monty-code-review skill and its SOLID reference to review this backend refactor. Call out coupling, contracts, and testability issues.

output_examples.input: A Django API change adds a new organization report endpoint.
output_examples.output: The review highlights correct serializer reuse, then flags missing tenant filtering, absent regression tests, and a contract risk in the response shape.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds several Django migrations for a large table.
output_examples.output: The review praises the model intent, then recommends a nullable column, batched backfill, and a follow-up constraint migration.

output_examples.input: A service refactor introduces new Slack and Teams reminder handlers.
output_examples.output: The review checks registry design, dependency injection, mock parity, and focused interfaces before giving a merge verdict.

best_practices: Provide the PR diff, business context, and any migration notes before asking for review.
Ask for a quick pass only when small style feedback would slow the review.
Run tests and linters after applying review suggestions.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a generic frontend or design review skill.
Do not ignore blocking tenant scoping, permission, or migration warnings.
Do not ask it to approve code without repository context.

faq.question: What languages does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Python and Django backend code, with emphasis on multi-tenant systems.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It may recommend or use available tooling, but test execution depends on the host environment and user request.

faq.question: Can it review migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Django migration safety, large tables, defaults, and staged rollouts.

faq.question: Can it do short reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for a quick pass to focus on blocking and should-fix issues.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes compatibility notes for Claude Code, Codex, and Claude.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a structured Markdown review with strengths, improvement items, test coverage notes, and a final verdict.
